exact_scope: Finite undirected graph with a deterministic v on every o-to-A path and every a_star-to-b path; event inclusion for any edge law, product probability bound for independent Bernoulli edges only.
independent_derivation: Concatenate the o-to-v prefix and v-to-b suffix. Harris association bounds the intersection of the two increasing events below by their probability product.
boundary_checks: Zero-length paths and probabilities 0 or 1 allowed; no conditional independence or probability-division argument.
remaining_gap: General graphs need not supply a separator witness; no general gluing conclusion.

exact_scope: Any finite forest, arbitrary independent Bernoulli edge probabilities, arbitrary o,b and nonempty A; coefficient 1 sharp.
independent_derivation: Remove trivial zero-right-side component cases, project relays onto the unique o-b path, and choose the nearest projection to o. It is the deterministic separator for L1. A two-edge path attains equality.
boundary_checks: Disconnected components, projection ties, o=b, A containing endpoints, and degenerate edge probabilities considered.
remaining_gap: A four-cycle has no such deterministic separator. This does not refute the general product inequality.

exact_scope: Arbitrary fixed relay order on path o--a2--a1--b, r,s,t in (0,1); both the individual preservation bridge and its incorrectly averaged unconditional version fail.
independent_derivation: I=a2 means first edge open and middle edge closed. Conditional terminal probability is 0. The actual probability rst is below the marginal average rst(2-s) by rst(1-s). The legitimate minimum-relay product remains exactly rst.
boundary_checks: For r=s=t=1/2 actual 1/8, marginal average 3/16, excess 1/16. Boundary s=1 removes the excess, as the strict assumptions predict.
remaining_gap: No refutation of the graph-uniform gluing conjecture or original critical target.
